instruction: Select all images containing a shoe.

game.semantic_variant: Select all things made to be worn on the feet.
game.hint: Select all that apply. If you are unsure, use your best judgement.
game.explanation: Ordinary shoes count, and so do the empty boots walking on wooden legs and the high heel standing on a human hand: impossible, but still shoes. The banana with laces and a sole and the horseshoe on a horse's hoof are borderline cases, recorded without a verdict. The handbag, the cycling helmet and the glove are not shoes.

correct: Shoes identified. Please wipe them on the way out.
Correct. Every pair has been matched.
partial: Partially correct. A shoe has gone missing, as they do.
Partially correct. One shoe was left behind.
incorrect: Incorrect. The Department will not be walked over.
Incorrect. Please step back and try again.

selection_review.reason: Nine distinct, standardised images reviewed together at tile size: two ordinary shoes (tan hand-tooled lace-up dress shoe, shallow three-quarter view; red child's wellington boot with a bunny print, side view), two impossible shoes (generated brown leather boots walking on jointed wooden mannequin legs; generated red court shoe whose heel is a human hand), two borderline items of footwear (generated banana with laces on a rubber sole; photographed horseshoe on a living horse's hoof) and three non-members that are also worn or carried (red and navy handbag, vented cycling helmet, worn yellow work glove). Leather and red appear among targets and non-members alike, so neither decides. Views, colours and settings vary within each role. The white trainer, the trainer on tiny trainers and the sock with a rubber sole remain in the collection for later versions.
